# SOP Audit: The Forge Belfast

**Gaps — no SOP yet**

- **Member Onboarding** – critical path missing; affects Day 1 experience, liability clarity, and retention momentum
- **Cancellation & Churn** – no documented win-back or exit-interview process; revenue leakage invisible
- **Member Checkins** – retention touchpoint undefined; unclear cadence, owner, triggers
- **Class Quality Audit Checklist** – no coaching standard enforcement mechanism; quality drifts undetected
- **Weekly Key Coach Tasks** – no role clarity on planning, prep, comms; creates bottlenecks
- **Coaching Development Roadmap** – no progression path for coaches; limits retention and consistency
- **Member data privacy & GDPR** – legal/compliance risk; data handling undocumented
- **Order Supplies & Sundries** – ad-hoc purchasing; cash flow and stock visibility poor
- **30 Day Goals & Member Outcomes** – no systematic tracking of results; weak proof-of-value for renewal
- **Referral Programme** – mechanics unclear; untapped revenue lever
- **Troubleshooting Guide** – common problems (booking glitches, payment fails, injury concerns) handled ad-hoc

**Needs updating**

- **Existing Coaches SOPs (19/22)** – likely missing: pre-class prep standards, post-class debrief/member follow-up, how to escalate safety concerns
- **Facilities SOPs (7/8)** – check coverage: opening/closing checklists, deep-clean schedules, equipment maintenance log and when to retire/replace gear
- **Clients SOPs (26/36)** – sparse; Milestone Achievements and Transformation Pillars absent; no framework for celebrating wins (boosts referrals and renewal intent)

# Service Menu Execution for The Forge

**1. Start with your revenue reality, not your dreams**
Pull your last 3 months of actual transactions. What ARE members actually buying? (Classes, PT, packages, add-ons?) Price those first—this is your foundation. Don't invent offerings; document what's working. This takes 2 hours max.

**2. Build TWO separate menus with brutal honesty**
- **Coach menu**: What can they actually deliver? (e.g., "small group PT = max 4 people, £35/session" not vague "personal training"). This prevents coaches over-promising and covers your liability.
- **Member menu**: Simplified version—only what they buy. Too many options kill conversions. Test: can a new member explain your pricing in 30 seconds?

**3. Price anchoring: use your premium tier to sell mid-tier**
Position your highest offering (e.g., "Elite 12-week body transformation, £1,200") FIRST. This makes your mid-tier (group coaching package, £400) look like the smart choice. Members don't want cheap; they want *value*.

**4. Embed this into ops immediately**
- Coaches get laminated cards (what they can offer + pricing—no negotiation)
- Members see it at signup, on your website, and on gym signage
- Set a review date: 30 days. What didn't sell? Kill it.

**5. Use this to train intake conversations**
Your coaches need a script: "Most members start with [mid-tier option], then add [add-on]." Make selling systematic, not uncomfortable.
